message.content: Both probe results are in and decisive: across ~99k adversarial rows per claim (full-bit-pattern FP16 search with directed cancellation selection down to <2⁻¹⁵ cancellation ratios, exact-zero-numerator rows, and extreme-value crosses), zero componentwise violations were found. Max error ratio 0.177 on both real and imag components, matching the theoretical bound (~a few ulps of FP32 relative error ≈ 2⁻²³ relative, vs the 5e-7 relative tolerance) — because the FP16×FP16 products are exact in FP32 and the sum's rounding error is ≤ half-ulp *of the sum itself*, the per-component relative error stays well under tolerance even under catastrophic cancellation. The observed worst rows (products ~65504 cancelling against ~1.07e9 partner with small scale) show ratio only 0.177. I'll finalize both claims as rebutted.

This matches theory: FP16xFP16 products are exact in FP32 and the FP32 sum rounding error is <= half-ulp of the sum itself, so the per-component relative error of the real component stays ~2^-23 < 5e-7 even under catastrophic cancellation.
